ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles 5-2, 5-3 and 5-4 of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information as amended effective November 1, 2024; Article 5-3 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act; Articles 8, 13 and 23 of the Commercial Act; Article 28 of the Local Tax Act; Articles 2-2 and 7 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Real Name Financial Transactions Act; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit examination standards; and FATF Recommendations 10 and 24.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at origin; affix Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the origin country only if that country is an Apostille Convention member. For non-member states, use consular legalization by the South Korean consulate in the origin state and do not attach an Apostille. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Existence of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: File registry or government business licensing authority of the shareholder's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize at origin; then affix Apostille by the origin country's competent authority if the origin state is a Hague Convention member. Otherwise, certify by the origin foreign ministry and legalize at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that state. Never combine Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution appointing in-country director and granting Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign corporate shareholder; notarized by a local notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a notary public in the jurisdiction of execution; Hague Apostille from the competent authority if that jurisdiction is an Apostille state; otherwise consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and incorporators, subsequently registered with the District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the Articles of Association are executed in Korea, no notarization may be needed for the filing itself, but a notarized and MOFA-apostilled copy can be produced for foreign bank use. If the articles contain foreign shareholder signatures, those signatures are notarized abroad and then Apostilled only if the origin state is an Apostille member; otherwise consular legalization applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the shareholder's existing bank or the Korean bank's pre-screening letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank of the foreign shareholder or the proposed Korean banking partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue a signed original on bank letterhead; the bank's signature is notarized and then Apostilled by the competent authority of the banking jurisdiction if an Apostille state; for non-member banks, the letter must be certified by the local foreign ministry and legalized by the Korean consulate. The paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the Korean court registry; for use inside Korea no further step is needed. For use abroad, a certified copy may be Apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; consular legalization is not required because Korea is an Apostille Convention member.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening under Korean AML rules must cover domestic and foreign politically exposed persons as defined in the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, all UN Security Council sanctions designations, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and sanctions programs, EU consolidated sanctions, Korean autonomous sanctions announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Interpol red notices, and credible adverse media. Matching must use full names, exact aliases, date of birth, passport and corporate registration numbers, jurisdiction, and address, with fuzzy logic for sound-alike names. Any PEP, sanctions, negative-media, or high proximity match requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and reporting to KoFIU if suspicious; refreshes occur every 90 days and upon ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Commercial Registration and Name Clearance System (i-REG portal) and National Tax Service HomeTax
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be written in Hangul; if a foreign-language brand is used, a phonetic Hangul transliteration is required. The naming convention has four tiers: distinguishing mark plus business object plus organizational form, ending with Chusik Hoesa. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered trade name; Roman letters may appear in trade publicity but cannot replace the registered Hangul name. Foreign words are transliterated according to their general pronunciation and are subject to the same prohibition against misleading similarity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After refusal, the applicant should submit a written objection to the registry court within 14 days, stating the rejection date, reference number, rejected name, and legal reasons under Articles 8, 10, 13 and 23 of the Commercial Act. The court will conduct a summary review; if denied, the applicant has 7 days for an immediate appeal to the appellate court. The applicant may simultaneously reserve a new name online through i-REG. The objection package must include the refusal notice, a proposed revised Hangul name, a legal memorandum showing no misleading similarity, and, if applicable, written consent of the existing name holder. A name reservation may be renewed once before expiry by filing a new reservation application and paying the small court refiling fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not statutorily prohibited but are operationally rejected by Korean banks and the National Tax Service for this industry. The National Tax Service requires an actual place of business under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act and Article 13 of the Enforcement Decree of the Income Tax Act, evidenced by a lease, signboard, inventory storage, personnel, telephone, and mail delivery. Banks will refuse corporate account opening for a used-machinery importer using a virtual office because KFIU-enhanced customer due diligence requires physical inspection and evidence of commercial substance. A virtual office is therefore not permissible as the sole compliance solution for a used construction excavator wholesale company transacting by wire transfer and SWIFT letters of credit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: registration office sign, original lease or ownership certificate, utility bills in company name, employee attendance records, business books, VAT invoices, customs declarations for imported used earthmovers, bank statements, and retained fixed-asset evidence. Quantified risk: 65% likelihood of an unannounced National Tax Service or municipal inspection within the first 12 months; 40% recurring annual likelihood thereafter; 90% likelihood where a virtual office or suspicious offshore ownership pattern is detected by the tax office or a bank.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and certified corporate registry extracts from i-REG
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea / District Court Registry Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Supreme Court fee schedule at approximately KRW 1,000 per extract copy

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration license tax and local education surcharge on stated capital of KRW 100,000,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Metropolitan or district local government revenue department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local Tax Act Article 28, 0.4% of stated capital plus 20% education surcharge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration filing fee and corporate seal registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court fee schedule for commercial registration and seal registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean legal fee for drafting Articles of Association, initial board resolutions, corporate filings, and power of attorney for foreign corporate shareholder
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Korean law firm fixed fee for a standard Chusik Hoesa incorporation with a foreign corporate shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation, notarization, and authentication of foreign shareholder documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation agency, Korean notary public, and foreign notary authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark page/hour rates for certified commercial translation plus notary fee schedule under Korean certification rules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization processing for origin-country corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section and competent authorities of the document's origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government fee where charged, plus courier and handling; Apostille for Hague states, consular legalization only for non-member states

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Tax Service business registration certificate and VAT registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is charged for business registration under Value-Added Tax Act Article 8; agent service fees are excluded

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter and pre-account KYC dossier preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Issuing bank and corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for authenticated letter plus corporate service provider hourly rate; not a government registry fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), especially Articles 288-294, 301, 317, 383, 388-393, 397-407 and 434; Framework Act on Foreign Investment; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Electronic Registration of Business Entities Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division); online portal I-reg under the Supreme Court of Korea; Business Registration Division of the competent District Tax Office for tax identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (legal name: chusik hoesa jeongwan) and the incorporation registration application (legal name: beobinseollip deunggi sincheongseo), filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act after the 2012 amendment. The Articles must state authorized capital and issued shares. Full payment of issued shares must be made to a blocked domestic Korean bank settlement account before registration, and the bank's capital deposit certificate is produced to the court. Funds are released only after completion of registration. Foreign investors using a non-resident entity should remit equity capital in KRW or permitted foreign currency and give prior report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act or the Foreign Investment Promotion Act if the statutory threshold is exceeded.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [ENTITY NAME], A CHUSIK HOESA, ADOPTED UNDER ARTICLE 393 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The Board of Directors (the Board) convened at the registered office on [date]. All directors constituting the full board were present and voted unanimously. After legal review, the Board resolved as follows: 1. Adoption of Articles of Incorporation: The Board accepts and adopts the Articles of Incorporation as notarized, including the object clause covering wholesale remarketing of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers, rollers, and related attachments, and confirms that the company is constituted as a stock corporation under Korean law. 2. Share Capital Subscription: The Board acknowledges receipt of subscriptions for [number] issued common shares with paid-up value of [amount] KRW per share, as shown on the subscription ledger and verified by the capital deposit certificate issued by the settlement bank. The Board confirms that all subscription proceeds are restrained from withdrawal until the registry issues the certificate of incorporation. 3. Banking and Cash Management Authorization: The Representative Director is authorized to open and operate demand deposit, foreign currency, settlement, and corporate investment accounts at one or more licensed Korean banks; to execute account signature mandates, online banking agreements, and anti-money-laundering declarations; and to negotiate credit facilities, letters of credit, and SWIFT payment arrangements necessary for used construction machinery trade. 4. Registered Office Adoption: The Board adopts [address] as the company's registered office and business place, authorizes execution and registration of the lease in the company's name, and directs the filing of the business registration with the competent District Tax Office immediately after court registration. 5. Statutory Officer Appointments: [Name] is appointed as the Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer with full power to represent the company in all affairs, including the execution of purchase and sale agreements for used excavators, customs declarations, import clearance filings, dealer registration applications, and regulatory submissions. [Name] is appointed as an Inside Director, and [Name] is appointed as the Auditor or Audit Committee member as elected in the incorporation particulars. The appointed officers accept their duties to convene general shareholders' meetings, preserve statutory books, and submit annual financial statements for shareholder approval. 6. General Ratification and Continuation: All lawful actions taken by the promoters and officers to organize the corporation, including notarization of the Articles, opening of the temporary capital account, and execution of lease documents, are hereby expressly ratified. The Board authorizes the issuance of certified extracts of this resolution to banks, courts, tax offices, customs authorities, and industrial licensing agencies for the continued operation and licensing of the company. This resolution is immediately effective and remains in force until amended by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Notarization of Articles and Share Subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court I-reg name reservation window, followed by a licensed Korean notary public under the Notary Public Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, place of registered office, precise object clause for wholesale remarketing of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers, total authorized shares, par value, initial issued shares, directors, auditor, and publication method. Reserve the corporate name on the I-reg portal to ensure no identical or confusingly similar registered name exists. All promoters must execute subscription applications identifying the number of shares taken and the amount paid. The notary must certify that the Articles are lawful and compatible with the Commercial Act. Foreign corporate founders must provide apostilled or consular-certified documents and certified Korean translations before the notary will authenticate the Articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Name reservation confirmation from I-reg
Passport or corporate registry extract of each promoter and intended director
Power of attorney with apostille or consular legalization
Subscription forms for all issued shares
Certified Korean translation of foreign documents and legalized corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reserved name is refused because of identical or confusingly similar existing names, select an alternative name in I-reg and amend the Articles before notarization. If the notary refuses certification because of incomplete foreign document legalization, obtain the missing apostille or consular certificate and a corrected sworn translation, then reschedule the notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit and Equity Payment Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Korean commercial bank licensed to accept corporate accounts (e.g., Shinhan, Woori, KB Kookmin, Hana, IBK), with mandatory reporting to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA or a foreign exchange bank where foreign equity remittance occurs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary share subscription settlement account in the name of the promoters or the company in formation. Wire or deposit the full subscription price for all issued shares from each shareholder's external or domestic account. Instruct the bank that the deposited funds are restricted from withdrawal until the court registration of incorporation is completed. The bank will issue a certificate of capital deposit or subscription payment confirmation showing the depositor name, amount, deposit date, and the withdrawal restriction. Simultaneously coordinate foreign investment reporting with KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank if the investing entity is foreign, regardless of whether the minimum statutory foreign investment threshold is met.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription forms
Capital remittance evidence or bank deposit slip
Passport or corporate documents of each subscriber
Beneficial ownership and anti-money-laundering declaration forms
Foreign exchange bank transaction confirmation for inward remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions the identity or source of funds, provide a certified corporate registry extract, audited financial statements, passport copies, and source-of-wealth statement. If the remittance is rejected or returned, resend using the same beneficiary and remitter with a corrected SWIFT reference. If the bank will not issue a restricted capital payment certificate, close the account and open a new blocked settlement account at another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the Competent District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office address (for Seoul: Seoul Central District Court), using the Supreme Court electronic registration portal I-reg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application together with the certified notarized Articles, the bank's capital deposit certificate, written acceptance of office by each director and auditor, the corporate seal impression certificate, and evidence of payment of court registration fees and local registration tax. The court registry will examine whether the Articles, capital payment, and appointments comply with the Commercial Act and the public registration law. Upon approval, the court assigns the corporate registration number and issues the certificate of incorporation registration. The company thus becomes a legal entity separate from its shareholders, with limited liability and capacity to open final bank accounts, execute contracts, and apply for operating permits.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application signed by the promoter or representative filer
Certified copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of capital deposit with no-dispersement notation
Written acceptance letters of all directors and the auditor
Corporate seal certificate and seal impression of the representative director
Passport or power of attorney of the electronic filer
Receipt of court filing fee and local education tax payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, comply within the specified ten-day period by filing amended Articles or supplemental evidence. If the registry refuses registration, an immediate appeal may be filed against the decision. For fatal defects, withdraw the pending application, cure the substantive issue, and re-file with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Competent District Tax Office and VAT Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS) with jurisdiction over the registered office, using the HomeTax digital portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the legally prescribed period after incorporation, file the Business Registration Application with the district tax office to obtain the corporate taxpayer identification number. Include the certificate of incorporation registration, corporate seal certificate, lease agreement or proof of registered office, and identification for the representative director. The business registration will cover corporate income tax, value-added tax, withholding tax, and electronic tax invoice obligations. For foreign investors, attach the foreign investment report or foreign exchange bank confirmation. Register the corporate bank accounts and the company's electronic tax invoice system to enable compliant invoicing for sales of used construction equipment.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Certificate of incorporation registration from the court
Corporate seal certificate and seal impression
Proof of registered office lease or ownership
Representative director identification and power of attorney
Foreign investment report acceptance or foreign exchange transaction certificate
VAT and electronic tax invoice registration questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district tax office queries the office address or representative identity, submit landlord's written consent, property tax certificate, and notarized power of attorney. If the company has no Korean-resident shareholder or director, appoint and register a local tax guarantor or tax representative if required, then re-file the business registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conditional Construction Machinery Dealer Registration and Import Clearance Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City Mayor or Provincial Governor (Do Governor) through the local si/gun/gu office under the Construction Machinery Management Act; Korea Customs Service and KOTRA for used imported equipment clearance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company will actually broker, wholesale, or physically sell secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers, file for construction machinery dealer registration with the local government before the first significant transaction. The application must demonstrate that the business premises, storage yard, and office are adequate and that the company will maintain construction machinery registration ledgers and transfer records. For imported used excavators, obtain used-goods import clearance under the Foreign Trade Act, ensure compliance with construction machinery registration and identification plate requirements, and declare the machinery to customs with original registration, hours meter readings, engine numbers, and emissions compliance evidence. The corporation must also maintain written sales contracts and ownership transfer records for each machine sold.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate from the NTS
Certificate of incorporation registration
Construction machinery dealer registration application
Lease or ownership proof of office and storage yard
Representative director identification and corporate seal certificate
Facility layout and safety equipment list
Foreign trade import clearance documents and customs declarations for imported units
Construction machinery registration certificate and ownership history records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local government returns the dealer registration application as incomplete, cure the specified deficiencies within the correction period and resubmit. If the registration is denied, request the written rejection reasons and file an administrative appeal with the provincial governor or an administrative court. If import clearance is suspended by customs, provide the manufacturer's origin certificate, dismantling/safety inspection records, and updated emissions data before re-submitting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City Mayor or Provincial Governor (Do Governor) acting through the local si/gun/gu office under the Construction Machinery Management Act; Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport for registration of construction machinery; Korea Customs Service for import clearance; National Fire Agency for premises fire safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as Construction Machinery Dealer (construction machinery sales business registration) under the Construction Machinery Management Act; supplemented by a used-goods import clearance for each imported excavator or roller under the Foreign Trade Act and customs procedures.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (ME) of the Republic of Korea, through provincial environmental offices and the Korea Environment Corporation; not applicable to the registered trading office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - EIA Exempt. The activity is wholesale trading and remarketing of used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers, not manufacturing, chemical processing, quarrying, or fixed industrial installation. Therefore no Full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, or Prior Environmental Review is required for the core office and dealer activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No quantitative discharge threshold applies to a pure trading operation. If occasional engine testing or maintenance inspection is performed at the sales yard, used lubricant, hydraulic oil, and oily waste must be segregated, labeled, and manifested to a licensed waste transporter under the Waste Control Act. Any accidental release of hydraulic oil into soil or water will trigger the Clean Water Act and Soil Environment Conservation Act remediation duties; therefore containment booms, spill kits, and drip pans are required at any machinery holding yard. Mobile compressors and any stationary test engines must comply with permissible emissions limits under the Clean Air Conservation Act, and imported machines must meet current diesel construction machinery emission standards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate for the registered office and any storage yard under the Fire Prevention and Safety Act, including accessible fire extinguishers, clearly marked exits, and electrical safety inspections. If the company maintains inventoried used excavators or rollers on an open yard, civil defense approval for the temporary storage layout, fire-break spacing, and emergency vehicle access is required from the local fire department. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the company must conduct a hazard assessment covering manual handling, machine movement, crushing hazards, and vehicle operations, and any employees engaged in equipment inspection must receive workplace safety training and personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic administration through the HomeTax portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr); export customs clearance and export declaration validation are handled electronically through the Korea Customs Service's UNI-PASS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa: (1) complete the Korean court registry incorporation and corporate registration; (2) apply for business registration through NTS HomeTax before commencing any taxable supply, selecting the principal domestic place of business in Korea; (3) submit the application together with the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, representative passport or national ID, and lease or ownership evidence of the Korean place of business; (4) receive the 10-digit registered business number from NTS, which serves as both the corporate TIN and VAT registration number; (5) obtain the business registration certificate. For a foreign non-resident entity with no Korean domestic place of business that nevertheless makes supplies taxable in Korea, the entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and file the same HomeTax business registration application using the foreign registry certificate, a notarized power of attorney to the tax representative, and the foreign entity's own TIN; NTS will issue a VAT registration number for that foreign entity. The Chusik Hoesa's Korean business number is also used for customs, e-tax invoices, and foreign exchange receipt reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Chusik Hoesa is a per-se stock corporation taxed at corporate entity level under the Korean Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through or disregarded-entity status is possible for a Korean incorporated Chusik Hoesa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election for domestically incorporated entities, and no hybrid-mismatch or partnership classification elections are available; the Chusik Hoesa remains a stand-alone corporate taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold: a person becomes a VAT-registered business operator from the first taxable supply of goods or services in Korea. The simplified taxable person regime for small individual enterprises with annual revenue below KRW 80,000,000 does not remove the registration obligation; it only changes the calculation and reporting burden.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B VAT supply transactions must be evidenced by tax invoices, and all registered business operators subject to e-invoicing must transmit the details as an electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) to NTS through the HomeTax system no later than the day following the date of the tax invoice. Integration is made through NTS-certified ERP platforms via HomeTax APIs, with data digitally signed by the taxpayer's certificate. Korea does not operate a pre-clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping model; instead, NTS performs automatic post-issuance cross-matching of e-tax invoices against customs export declarations and foreign exchange receipt data to detect false zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero rate applies when used construction excavators, hydraulic shovels, and rollers are physically exported from Korea to a foreign buyer and the Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa is the seller and declarant in its own name. To substantiate the 0% VAT rate, the exporter must hold a valid export customs declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service, issue a zero-rated electronic tax invoice through HomeTax, transport the goods out of Korea, and collect the export proceeds in foreign currency within the statutory export-proceeds collection period. Domestic sale in Korea or deemed export to a non-exporting domestic purchaser is subject to 10% VAT, unless the transaction is restructured as an actual zero-rated export followed by physical exportation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export declaration confirmation (outbound shipment) obtained from the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS electronic export clearance system, showing the Chusik Hoesa as seller and exporter and the used construction machinery being cleared for export
Commercial invoice and packing list with the used equipment details, serial numbers, condition, and HS classification for hydraulic excavators and rollers
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of the used machinery from Korea to the foreign destination

Certificate of Export Proceeds Receipt (Foreign Exchange Receipt Confirmation) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, evidencing payment collection in foreign currency
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice transmitted to NTS HomeTax, linked to the export customs declaration reference number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS will verify each zero-rated export by matching the e-tax invoice to the customs export declaration and the foreign exchange receipt within the 180-day repatriation window. Failure to export, failure to collect proceeds on time, or defective documentation will reverse the zero rating and cause NTS to assess 10% VAT on the full invoice amount, plus interest and VAT additional tax penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Where the exporter knowingly files false export declarations, forges customs or foreign exchange receipts, or colludes in the issuance of fictitious e-tax invoices, criminal liability can be asserted under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act against the representative and related persons, together with confiscation and collection of the evaded VAT, penalties, and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and coordinated with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Customs Service for enforcement and delegated authorization of foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized current-account foreign exchange regime. Trade-related payments, dividends, interest, and royalties can be converted and remitted through authorized foreign exchange banks upon submission of supporting documentation. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity investment, acquisition of foreign assets, and loans, are liberalized but subject to mandatory reporting and, where applicable, prior registration with a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. There is no blanket surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in foreign-currency accounts or convert to Korean won at a market rate. The practical hurdle for profit remittance from a Chusik Hoesa is the need to evidence accrued and distributable profits through audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance certificates, and a board resolution, together with a foreign investor registration certificate and a valid foreign exchange bank account linked to the foreign investment report. Inflows for used excavator trading require precise declaration of the purpose code and underlying sale-purchase contracts to avoid classification as a suspicious outbound remittance. Domestic banks perform real-time transaction monitoring and may require invoices to be validated by customs declarations. While the Korean won participates in the CLS settlement system only indirectly and is not freely tradable offshore outside controlled interbank channels, current-account convertibility is practically unencumbered for tax-compliant entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory export proceeds collection period under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is 15 months from the date of export declaration. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter may hold the proceeds in an authorized foreign currency account or sell them to a foreign exchange bank at the spot rate. Bank-issued foreign exchange transaction records must be kept for five years and be presented for tax and customs audits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Corporate Operating Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Corporate Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Registration) and Export Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and USD/EUR Clearing Account
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Finance Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low - Legally non-viable as primary banking rail. Non-bank fintech EMIs and offshore digital wallets do not hold a domestic banking license and are not permitted to open corporate accounts or facilitate foreign exchange transactions in South Korea. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires all payments, conversions, and collection of export proceeds to be handled through a local authorized foreign exchange bank. Such EMIs may only provide supplementary expense management interfaces if they are linked to an underlying licensed bank account; they cannot replace the corporate treasury structure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one registered director or a formally appointed signatory with a power of attorney certified by the Korean consulate must appear physically in branch for the initial corporate onboarding. Remote video-call KYC is not accepted for a medium-risk enhanced trade profile involving secondhand heavy machinery. The director must present original passport, corporate seal certificate, and recent residence proof. If the director is a non-resident, a locally resident compliance officer may be appointed for certain banks, but the statutory representative must still complete one in-branch verification unless the bank expressly permits consular attestation mail-in due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by foreign shareholders and tiered holding structures in a Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Commercial Registry, articles of incorporation, current shareholder register, UBO declaration identifying every natural person with shareholding above 25%, passports and tax numbers for each UBO, an ownership-chain diagram, source-of-wealth statement, and a resolution of the board designating a local AML representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering signals from secondhand excavator import/export, including over/under-invoicing or false valuation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices and purchase contracts, Korea Customs Service export/import declarations, bill of lading with full container/equipment serial numbers, third-party valuation certificate from an approved heavy machinery appraiser, equipment condition/pre-sale inspection reports, marine insurance policies, and proof of disposal of prior cargo by serial number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden large inward payments from gray-market or offshore jurisdictions without clear underlying trade rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty due diligence file with beneficial ownership names and registration documents, sanctioned and PEP screening results from OFAC, EU, UN, US BIS, and Korean FSS lists, original SWIFT confirmation, transaction-specific board resolution, warehouse/reconsignment agreements, and movement tracking from the port of shipment to final delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between declared ISIC 4659 trading activity and actual transaction value or frequency of non-trade SWIFT flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Categorized bank statements in the first six months, floor/collateral lease agreements, logistics contracts with licensed haulers, inventory and VIN/serial tracking record, periodic financial statements, and a description of internal controls that review every payment against the underlying customs stamp and bill of lading.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must report a foreign investment of over KRW 300 million using the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through a designated local bank. A foreign-currency capital escrow account is opened, and the remitter wires funds with the bank-provided reference and purpose code 'Flow in of foreign direct investment'. After confirmation and receipt, the bank issues a foreign investment certificate, and the funds are converted into KRW. Capital verification is completed through the auditor's report and the bank's foreign exchange transaction record.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payment for used excavator purchases abroad is executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfer with the purpose code for import of goods, supported by the pro-forma invoice. For transactions exceeding banks' interest threshold, an Import Letter of Credit (Incoterms based) or a documentary collection may be used to protect both parties. Export remittances to overseas buyers are processed only after presenting the Korea Customs Service export declaration, invoice, and transport document for the same transaction reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Notional forward foreign exchange contracts with licensed banks for trade receivables and payables up to 180 days with underlying commercial documentation
Onshore currency options (vanilla and barrier options) for genuine current-account hedge exposures
Cross-currency interest rate swaps limited to permitted long-term external borrowing
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions are allowed only for foreign institutional counterparties outside Korea, not for domestic operating entities, unless specifically approved by Bank of Korea

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders - statutory presentation, deliberation and approval of annual financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporation's registered office minutes; no government filing unless court-registered officer changes arise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, no later than March 31 of the following year; notice to shareholders must be given at least two weeks before the meeting; the shareholder register may be closed for no more than three months prior to the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM exposes directors to an administrative negligence fine of up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,700); shareholders may petition the court for an order convening the meeting; non-approval of audited accounts impairs dividend distributions and statutory profit distribution documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax final return with financial statements, adjustment schedules, reserves and profit disposition ledgers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax electronic filing; District Tax Office for the registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; calendar-year companies must file by March 31, except that a return prepared and certified by a licensed tax accountant or CPA may be filed by April 30 under the Corporate Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or omission attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax; understatement triggers 10% additional tax with aggravated penalties for intentional false returns; overdue corporate tax accrues daily additional interest of 0.025% (approx. 9.125% per annum); prolonged non-payment permits enforced seizure and cancellation of the business tax registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Principal local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Wetax e-filing system administered by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax: within three months after fiscal year-end; March 31 for calendar-year companies (April 30 if the corporate return is prepared by a licensed tax agent or CPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of the local corporate tax return imposes 20% additional tax on the local tax payable; understatement imposes 10%; overdue local tax accrues 0.025% per day (approx. 9.125% per annum); enforcement and asset seizure follow sustained non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT final returns for the two semi-annual taxable periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January 1 to June 30) return due July 25; second half (July 1 to December 31) return due January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file VAT imposes 20% additional tax on the payable VAT; understatement or excess input credit imposes 10%; late-paid VAT accrues 0.025% per day (approx. 9.125% per annum); sustained delinquency can trigger forfeiture of refund rights, business registration cancellation, and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and independent auditor's report filed to FSS/DART for statutory audit subjects
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / Securities and Futures Commission through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year audit subjects, audited financial statements must be approved at the AGM by March 31; the approved annual report, audited financial statements and auditor's opinion are filed to FSS/DART within two weeks after AGM approval (composite deadline in April, generally before the corporate tax expiration date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Refusal to appoint a licensed external auditor is sanctionable under the External Audit Act, with fines up to KRW 50 million (approx. USD 37,000); non-filing of the auditor's report triggers FSS administrative sanctions, designation of an ex-officio auditor, public non-compliance disclosure, and adverse credit standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial-register health check and mandatory registration of post-AGM officer changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Court Registration Office through the Commercial Register Portal under the Korean Supreme Court Registration Information Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual date for the health check, but any change in directors, representative, registered office, articles of incorporation, or share transfer restrictions must be court-registered within 14 calendar days of the event; for calendar-year companies the annual reconciliation is completed immediately after the AGM and no later than April 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late court registration is subject to a negligence fine of up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,700) under the Commercial Act; an unregistered resolution or director appointment cannot be asserted against a good-faith third party; the court may order compulsory registration and continuing noncompliance can lead to administrative closure of the registration entry after demand notices.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is legally required to appoint a licensed CPA auditor and file a certified audit report if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, it meets any of the following quantitative benchmarks: (i) total assets of KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.1 million) or more; (ii) total assets of KRW 2 billion or more together with 1,000 or more registered shareholders or widely dispersed shareholdings; (iii) it is a listed company, a bank, an insurance company, a securities company, a financial investment company, or other financial/payment institution designated by law regardless of asset size; or (iv) the Financial Supervisory Service has specifically designated the company as an external audit target because of dispersed ownership, public interest, or materially false unaudited financial statements. The FSS may also apply an employee/revenue adverse-selection test to large unlisted SMEs, and an SME statutory exemption is lost for companies exceeding the applicable asset, 100-employee, or KRW 10 billion revenue thresholds prescribed by the Enforcement Decree.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) as issued by the Korea Accounting Standards Board is mandatory for listed and publicly designated financial entities; a non-listed Chusik Hoesa may apply K-GAAP (General Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises) or voluntarily adopt K-IFRS. Inventory of used construction excavators must be measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value, and revenue recognition must comply with the applicable K-IFRS 15 equivalent or K-GAAP revenue standard for wholesale trading of heavy machinery.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not require an annual UBO return to a central corporate registry for a private Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial ownership is evidenced through the Registered Shareholders Register maintained at the registered office, and every share transfer must be entered in that register before the transfer is effective against the company. Before the AGM the board may fix a record date and close the register for a period not exceeding three months, typically 30 calendar days. Where a foreign investor holds at least 10% of shares or has de facto control, any acquisition or disposal transaction must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to the Foreign Investment Service Center within 30 days of the transaction date. Financial institutions and trade counterparties involved in wire-transfer or documentary-credit settlements will require KYC and beneficial-owner identification records, which the company must retain for at least 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Current Officers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% top marginal (progressive: 10% up to KRW 200M; 20% from KRW 200M to KRW 20B; 22% from KRW 20B to KRW 300B; 25% above KRW 300B) plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act including R&D expense credits up to 25% of qualifying expenses, job creation credits, and new growth facility investment credits; foreign-invested enterprise incentives in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones (up to 100% exemption for five years plus 50% for two additional years); patent box-like partial income exclusion for qualifying patented IP; special SME tax reductions for the first five years for enterprises incorporated in Korea; used heavy machinery trading may benefit from the asset acquisition tax exemption for machinery used in FEA projects but does not enjoy automatic profit exemption outside designated zones

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Base Calculation (Form 1) under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act; mandatory electronic filing through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) using an approved digital certificate
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year entities: by March 31 of the following year); two semi-annual interim tax prepayments are also due within two months after the end of the first six months (e.g., August 31 for calendar-year filers)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, fiscal year-end, industry code, and representative director details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the percentage and identity of every non-resident shareholder in the shareholder register schedule; attach a foreign ownership statement so that dividends paid or deemed paid to non-residents are traceable for withholding purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and income statement summary derived from the statutory audit of the financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure all purchases of used hydraulic excavators and rollers from foreign related suppliers are separately itemized on the gross profit reconciliation sheet; import customs value must align with the arm's-length transfer price and with paid customs duties; any discrepancy triggers an audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from wholesale remarketing sales of used construction earthmovers and rollers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all export revenues from sales to foreign distributors; for intercompany export sales, apply the selected transfer pricing method and disclose the transactional net margin in Annex TP; do not omit incidental income from inspection commissions, freight reimbursement, or after-sale repair services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible cost of goods sold, selling, general and administrative expenses, and non-operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate every payment to non-residents for machinery appraisal, freight forwarding, auction fees, or technology licensing; if a payment includes embedded rights to use brand or technical knowledge, split out a notional royalty and confirm that 20% domestic withholding tax plus 2% local surtax has been withheld, unless treaty-reduced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before special deductions and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back all non-deductible items: excess entertainment expenses, donations exceeding statutory ceilings, criminal fines, and deemed interest arising from thin capitalisation on loans from non-resident shareholders (debt-to-equity ratio 3:1 generally; 6:1 for financial institutions); apply the restriction on interest deduction to excessive related-party borrowings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special deductions and tax credits: R&D, foreign tax credit, investment tax credit, and loss carryforward deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits for withholding taxes imposed by the country of origin on used machinery resale income when Korea taxes the same foreign-source income; attach Form 11 with a certified Tax Residency Certificate and evidence of actual foreign tax paid; losses may be carried forward fifteen years, but require full documentation of the composition of the loss (only business and investment losses qualify).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax computation at progressive rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate national tax using the progressive bands for the current year; then compute 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax amount; the combined effective tax rate is 11% on the first KRW 200M of taxable income up to 27.5% on income above KRW 300B.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of prepayments, withholding tax credits, interim tax payments, and net tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident payees in the attached withholding schedule; even if no corporate tax is payable due to losses, full filing is mandatory to avoid 20% non-filing penalty and to preserve tax loss carryforwards; certify that all outbound remittances have been made through a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank with withholding evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% penalty on the underpaid tax under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; fraudulent under-reporting triggers a 40% penalty under Article 47-2; negligent under-reporting is penalized at 10%; non-payment or short-payment of the assessed amount accrues daily surcharge interest of 0.022% per day from the due date; failure to withhold or remit non-resident withholding tax exposes the payer to 100% of the unremitted amount plus a fine; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can raise penalties to imprisonment up to five years or a fine equal to twice the evaded tax when the evasion exceeds KRW 300M.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge = 22% statutory dividend withholding tax on cash or deemed dividends paid to non-resident corporations and individuals; treaty rates (typically 5% for 10%+ shareholders and 15% otherwise) may reduce this where the applicable DTA is claimed
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty reduced withholding, the non-resident payee must submit before or at the time of remittance: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the treaty state; (2) a Beneficial Ownership Declaration demonstrating legal and economic entitlement to the income, with supporting proof of active business or investment substance; (3) a Foreign Shareholding Certificate evidencing the number and holding period of shares (where DTA requires at least certain ownership percentage); and (4) the Korean withholding agent must file Form 14-1 ('Application for Tax Treaty Limitation on Tax Rates') through HomeTax. If the reduced rate is not applied at source, the non-resident must file an amended return or Request for Formal Adjustment within three years of the due date under Article 45 of the Framework Act. The Korean tax authority may deny relief if the recipient is a conduit entity in a no-tax or low-tax jurisdiction without real economic functions, regardless of TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 20% national + 2% local = 22%; royalties / industrial property fees 20% + 2% = 22% if used in Korea. Treaty rates under Korea's comprehensive DTA network generally reduce interest to 10%-15%, royalties to 5%-15% for cultural/industrial IP, and business profits to zero if no permanent establishment exists. For used machinery trading, amounts paid for software embedded in equipment, technical know-how, or licensed inspection algorithms must be segregated from the goods price and subjected to the royalty withholding regime; contingent consideration for the right to remarket in a designated territory may be treated as a royalty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5M) in aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions triggers mandatory preparation and submission of Transfer Pricing Master File and Local File; simpler 'Simplified TP Document' is required when related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion with any single foreign related party, even when the aggregate threshold is not met; tax authorities may request contemporaneous evidence within 30 days regardless of threshold if audit risk is identified.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulation filing regime but applies the substance-over-form doctrine codified in Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the beneficial ownership rules of the International Tax Adjustment Act. A Korean Chusik Hoesa acting as a mere letterbox for a non-resident principal will be disregarded: the non-resident is deemed to have a Korean permanent establishment if core income-generating activities (negotiation, storage of used excavator inventory, inspection, assumption of risk, and title transfer) occur in the Korean jurisdiction. For treaty relief, CIGA must be demonstrable through physical offices, locally employed managers, actual purchasing/licensing contracts, and bank accounts. The absence of such substance exposes the entity to foreign-controlled domestic corporation recharacterization, disallowance of expenses, and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion via Falsified Import Cost Base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically importing used hydraulic excavators and rollers using artificially inflated invoices from a related foreign shell supplier located in a no-tax or low-tax jurisdiction, while actual economic ownership and damage risk already transfer to the Korean Chusik Hoesa, thereby inflating deductible cost of goods sold and understating Korean taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to 2x evaded tax); Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes (fraudulent understatement penalty of 40% of the underpaid tax); Article 6 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (arm's length adjustment plus 10% of the adjusted income as additional penalty); Customs Law penalties for false declaration of import value (fine up to 5x the evaded duty and criminal liability for customs fraud).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean appellate courts pierce the corporate veil when the company is used as a fraud instrument or the director acts in a grossly negligent manner. The representative director may be jointly and severally liable for the entire underpaid corporate tax under Article 39 of the Framework Act; personal assets can be attached; a departure ban is issued under Article 33 of the National Tax Collection Act; criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to five years; the company and director are blacklisted from government procurement and foreign trade license renewal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany sales of used excavators to a foreign related distributor at prices materially below arm's-length, compounded by failure to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File once aggregate cross-border related-party turnover reaches KRW 10 billion; the investigation shows that after-tax profits were accumulated in a tax haven while the Korean entity earned systematically low margins and no economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Article 6 (arm's length adjustment); Article 7 (secondary adjustment on deemed dividend or loan if profits are artificially retained abroad); Article 13 (non-submission of documentation: fine up to KRW 200 million); Article 34 (successive penalty charge of 30% of the understated taxable income attributable to undisclosed related-party transactions); Framework Act Article 47-3 for non-filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The tax authority may assert a collection against the director as a responsible manager where the director signed the TP documentation or knowingly approved the non-arm's-length price. Court doctrine permits veil-piercing in egregious cases, exposing rent house and personal bank accounts. A criminal charge under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may be filed, with imprisonment up to five years; the director faces personal civil-liability restitution and disqualification from serving as a director of any Korean corporation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping Through Non-Beneficial Ownership and Shell Shareholder
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident shareholder interposes a Singapore or Hong Kong nominee holding company to receive dividends from the Korean Chusik Hoesa, claiming a 10% DTA withholding rate while the actual beneficial owner is a Korean resident or a third-country national; the Korean entity pays dividends with the reduced rate but fails to obtain the mandatory TRC and beneficial ownership declaration, and the holding company performs no substantive function beyond receiving dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 17-3 of the International Tax Adjustment Act (denial of treaty relief where the recipient is not beneficial owner); Article 24 of the same Act (disallowance of tax avoidance arrangements); the tax authority imposes domestic 22% withholding on the gross dividend plus 0.022% daily overdue interest; Framework Act Article 47-2 imposes 40% false-report penalty on the withholding agent; the foreign shareholder may be sanctioned with a fine equal to the under-withheld amount and interest. If the scheme includes forged TRC, criminal sanction under Article 3-2 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act applies (imprisonment up to five years).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally structured the conduit arrangement are jointly and severally liable for the differential withholding tax; the corporate veil is pierced on grounds of abuse of legal personality; the Korean director and the foreign beneficial owner haves their assets frozen, travel bans issued, and are extraditable under the relevant tax mutual assistance treaty; imprisonment up to five years is available, with additional civil restitution for tax revenue loss; the foreign shareholder is also barred from future dividend remittances until the unpaid withholding is fully settled.
